title: Telescoping criterion for a homogeneous submodule
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $n\in\mathbf N$, and $\ell>0$. In $A[Y_1,\ldots,Y_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], let $V_\ell$ be the $A$-submodule of polynomials all of whose nonzero monomials have total degree $\ell$, and let $S\subseteq V_\ell$ be an $A$-submodule. For $0\le r\le n$ let $\rho_r$ set the first $r$ variables equal to zero. Suppose that for every $0\le r<n$ and every $P\in V_\ell\cap A[Y_{r+1},\ldots,Y_n]$ divisible by $Y_{r+1}$ there is $Q\in S$ such that $\rho_r(Q)=P$. Then each such $P$ belongs to $S$, and $S=V_\ell$. More precisely, for every $T\in V_\ell$ the polynomials $T_j=\rho_{j-1}(T)-\rho_j(T)$, $1\le j\le n$, belong to $S\cap A[Y_j,\ldots,Y_n]$, are divisible by $Y_j$, and satisfy $T=\sum_{j=1}^nT_j$. The hypotheses and conclusions include $n=0$ and the zero ring.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 for the inherited route; Bierstone--Milman, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), Proof of Theorem 8.1 after Lemma 8.5, printed p.275: triangular induction and telescoping coordinate restrictions, isolated for an arbitrary homogeneous submodule. Journal PDF read online at https://mahalex.net/seminars/gabber/Bierstone-Milman%20Canonical%20desingularization%20in%20characteristic%20zero.pdf. No Stacks tag states this specialized result; BM paper absent from repository literature.

proof.text: By the coefficient description in [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], write $U=\sum_{|\alpha|=\ell}c_\alpha Y^\alpha$ with finite support. Evaluation gives $\rho_r(U)=\sum_{|\alpha|=\ell,\ \alpha_1=\cdots=\alpha_r=0}c_\alpha Y^\alpha$. Thus $D_j(U):=\rho_{j-1}(U)-\rho_j(U)$ is exactly the sum over $\alpha_1=\cdots=\alpha_{j-1}=0$ and $\alpha_j>0$. It lies in $V_\ell\cap A[Y_j,\ldots,Y_n]$ and equals $Y_j\sum c_\alpha Y^{\alpha-e_j}$ over those indices, proving divisibility without cancellation or division of coefficients.

source.place: Bierstone--Milman, Canonical desingularization in characteristic zero, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), p.275, proof of Theorem 8.1 after Lemma 8.5; agent-written arbitrary-submodule specialization.

proof.text: For $0\le r<n$, let $H(r)$ assert that every $P\in V_\ell\cap A[Y_{r+1},\ldots,Y_n]$ divisible by $Y_{r+1}$ belongs to $S$. Prove $H(r)$ by strong induction on $r$. For $r=0$ the assumed lift $Q\in S$ satisfies $Q=\rho_0(Q)=P$, so $P\in S$.

source.place: Bierstone--Milman, Canonical desingularization in characteristic zero, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), p.275, proof of Theorem 8.1 after Lemma 8.5; agent-written arbitrary-submodule specialization.

proof.text: Let $0<r<n$ and assume $H(s)$ for all $s<r$. For a $P$ as in $H(r)$ choose the stipulated $Q\in S$ with $\rho_r(Q)=P$. Since $S\subseteq V_\ell$, Step 1 applies to $Q$. For $1\le j\le r$, its $D_j(Q)$ has precisely the hypotheses of $H(j-1)$, so $D_j(Q)\in S$. The finite sum cancels consecutive restrictions: $\sum_{j=1}^rD_j(Q)=Q-\rho_r(Q)=Q-P$. Consequently $P=Q-\sum_{j=1}^rD_j(Q)\in S$, using closure of the submodule under addition and negation. This proves the induction step and all $H(r)$.

source.place: Bierstone--Milman, Canonical desingularization in characteristic zero, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), p.275, proof of Theorem 8.1 after Lemma 8.5; agent-written arbitrary-submodule specialization.

proof.text: For $T\in V_\ell$ and $1\le j\le n$, Step 1 and $H(j-1)$ give $T_j=D_j(T)\in S\cap A[Y_j,\ldots,Y_n]$ and $Y_j\mid T_j$. Adding gives $\sum_{j=1}^nT_j=T-\rho_n(T)$. After setting all variables to zero only the constant coefficient survives; it is zero since $\ell>0$. Hence $T=\sum_jT_j\in S$, so $V_\ell\subseteq S$, and the reverse inclusion is assumed. If $n=0$, there is no monomial of positive degree, so $V_\ell=S=0$ and the sum is empty. In the zero ring every coefficient is zero, and the same arguments apply.

source.place: Bierstone--Milman, Canonical desingularization in characteristic zero, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), p.275, proof of Theorem 8.1 after Lemma 8.5; agent-written arbitrary-submodule specialization.

lean.statement: theorem homogeneous_coordinate_lifting_criterion {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (n ℓ : ℕ) (hℓ : 0 < ℓ) (S : Submodule A (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A)) (hS : S ≤ homogeneousSubmodule (Fin n) A ℓ) (hLift : ∀ (r : Fin n) (P : MvPolynomial (Fin n) A), P ∈ homogeneousSubmodule (Fin n) A ℓ → P ∈ supported A {i : Fin n | r.val ≤ i.val} → X r ∣ P → ∃ Q ∈ S, aeval (fun i : Fin n ↦ if i.val < r.val then 0 else X i) Q = P) : (∀ (r : Fin n) (P : MvPolynomial (Fin n) A), P ∈ homogeneousSubmodule (Fin n) A ℓ → P ∈ supported A {i : Fin n | r.val ≤ i.val} → X r ∣ P → P ∈ S) ∧ S = homogeneousSubmodule (Fin n) A ℓ ∧ ∀ (T : MvPolynomial (Fin n) A), T ∈ homogeneousSubmodule (Fin n) A ℓ → (∀ j : Fin n, (aeval (fun i : Fin n ↦ if i.val < j.val then 0 else X i) T - aeval (fun i : Fin n ↦ if i.val < j.val + 1 then 0 else X i) T) ∈ S ∧ (aeval (fun i : Fin n ↦ if i.val < j.val then 0 else X i) T - aeval (fun i : Fin n ↦ if i.val < j.val + 1 then 0 else X i) T) ∈ supported A {i : Fin n | j.val ≤ i.val} ∧ (X j : MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) ∣ (aeval (fun i : Fin n ↦ if i.val < j.val then 0 else X i) T - aeval (fun i : Fin n ↦ if i.val < j.val + 1 then 0 else X i) T)) ∧ T = ∑ j : Fin n, (aeval (fun i : Fin n ↦ if i.val < j.val then 0 else X i) T - aeval (fun i : Fin n ↦ if i.val < j.val + 1 then 0 else X i) T)
